definition: Reiterate means to say or state something again, usually for emphasis or clarity.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word reiterate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know reiterate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The guide had set the turnaround time at breakfast; on the ridge she paused to reiterate it: whatever the summit looked like, the group would turn back at noon.
To mention a point is to raise it once in passing; to reiterate is to return to it deliberately, a second time, for emphasis.
To hammer a point home is to reiterate it so relentlessly that no listener can escape it.

Restate means to say something again in clearer or different words, so that it lands better or is finally understood — restating aims at clarity. Reiterate aims at force: the same point, stated again to give it weight or remove doubt. You restate a rule a student misheard; you reiterate a rule people keep testing.

Repeat is the all-purpose word for saying or doing something again, for any reason at all — an echo, a chorus, a rerun. Reiterate is deliberate and rhetorical: a speaker returns to a point already made, specifically to press it. Recordings and parrots repeat; only someone driving a point home reiterates.

Underscore means to stress a point so it stands out — and you can underscore something the very first time you say it, with a pause, a statistic, or a raised voice. Reiterate requires a second telling: its emphasis comes from saying the thing again. Underscoring highlights; reiterating repeats.

Use reiterate when someone states again what has already been said, usually to add emphasis or remove doubt: a spokesperson will reiterate a denial, a memo will reiterate a deadline.

At the noon briefing, Chief Alvarez read it again, unchanged: leave by Route 9; do not wait for the smoke.
A reporter asked why she kept returning to instructions everyone had already received.
'Because people bargain with a fire,' she said.
'They hear an order once and treat it as a suggestion.' So she would reiterate it at every briefing — the same nine words, in the same order — until the ridge was empty.
